s7-b1.stdout:
We counted warp breaks on 54 looms, each weaving the same length of
yarn, and modelled the counts with a quasi-Poisson regression on
wool and tension, because their variance was about 4.3 times what a
Poisson model allows. For the same wool, looms at high tension had
40.5% fewer breaks than at low tension (95% CI 23.1% to 54.2%
fewer), and looms at medium tension 27.5% fewer (7.6% to 43.3%
fewer). Wool B had 18.6% fewer breaks than wool A, but the interval
runs from 34.0% fewer to 0.2% more, so these data cannot settle
whether the wools differ. The model assumes tension has the same
proportional effect on both wools. It expects about 40 breaks per
loom (95% CI 33 to 48) for wool A at low tension, and about 19 (15
to 25) for wool B at high tension.
